scope: Round 19: cache the FAQ and its answers in Redis. The Node API owns Redis (Flask in be/rag still never opens a database or Redis; it goes through call_api to /api/rag/* with the internal token). FAQ entries live in Postgres (soft delete) and are served through a new FAQ API, cache-aside from Redis. The chat bot answers a question that matches an FAQ from the cache without calling Gemini; every other question goes through the existing RAG pipeline unchanged. Redis is never required for correctness: when it is down, every read falls back to Postgres and the chat falls back to RAG. One feature per step, id faq-cache-<n>. Standing SRS rules: unit and integration tests in the e2e folder (e2e/unit, e2e/integration, e2e/py; this SRS no longer asks for Playwright e2e specs), changed files described in docs/changes/, all delete means soft delete.

source_requirements.text: SRS.txt 2026-11-20: system - caching FAQ with redis. Build a feature_list for caching FAQ and answer with redis. Req-1: build on backend side. Req-2: FAQ API handle. Req-3: Keep Rag pipeline continue.

features.title: Run Redis and give the API a fail-open cache client
features.user_visible_behavior: No visible change. docker compose also starts Redis; the API can read and write cache keys, and keeps working when Redis is down.

Add REDIS_URL to be/src/config.ts and be/.env.example (default redis://127.0.0.1:6380/0). Tests use their own database index (auction_test -> /1, auction_e2e -> /2) so runs never see dev keys.

Add the official redis npm client to be/ and one module be/src/lib/cache.ts exposing get/set(ttl)/del/delByPrefix with JSON values and a key prefix. Every call catches Redis errors, logs once, and returns null / does nothing (fail-open) with a short connect timeout so a dead Redis never blocks a request.

Same test with REDIS_URL pointing at a closed port: get returns null and set resolves within 1 s without throwing.

verification: Add be/src/routes/faqs.ts mounted at /api/faqs. GET /:id does the same with faq:item:<id>; unknown or deleted id -> 404.
Each response carries X-Cache: HIT or MISS so tests and ops can see the cache working.

features.title: Internal FAQ match endpoint for the chat bot
features.user_visible_behavior: No visible change. Flask can ask Node whether a chat question is a known FAQ and get its answer from Redis.
verification: Add GET /api/rag/faq-match?q= in be/src/routes/rag.ts behind requireInternal. It normalizes q, reads faq:q:<sha256(normalized)> from Redis; on a miss it looks up Faq.normalizedQuestion in Postgres and caches the hit (and a short-TTL negative entry for a miss, so repeated unknown questions do not hit Postgres each time).
Answers 200 {faqId, question, answer} on a match, 404 on no match, 400 on an empty or over-long q.

e2e/integration/faq-cache-5-match.test.ts: an exact FAQ question and the same question with different case, spacing and a missing '?' both match; second call served from Redis (spy or key check); an edited FAQ answer is returned right after the edit; a deleted FAQ no longer matches; missing internal token 401.

2026-11-20 e2e/integration/faq-cache-5-match.test.ts 5/5: exact + loose spelling match, second call HIT; miss 404 remembered; new FAQ matches right after a remembered miss; edit returned at once; deleted 404; 400 empty/blank/missing/over 4000; 401 missing/wrong token.

features.notes: Exact match on the normalized question only. Fuzzy or embedding similarity is out of scope: questions that do not match exactly go to RAG, which already retrieves FAQ-like knowledge.

features.title: Cache RAG answers to repeated guest questions
features.user_visible_behavior: A guest asking a question that was already answered recently gets the same answer faster; answers are refreshed when the bot's documents or FAQs change.
verification: Only guest turns are cached: a signed-in visitor's prompt contains their bids, lots and credit (build_prompt._account), so their answers are never stored or served from cache.

Only outcome answered with no guard reason is stored. Key rag:ans:<knowledge version>:<sha256(normalized question)>, TTL RAG_ANSWER_TTL_SECONDS (default 86400). Node exposes GET and PUT /api/rag/answer-cache behind requireInternal; Flask uses them through one function file.
The knowledge version key rag:ver is bumped when a document is uploaded or deleted (existing /api/docs routes in Node) and on any FAQ write, so old answers stop matching at once.
A cache hit is still logged as a turn (model 'rag-cache') with the cached sources.

e2e/py/faq_cache_7_answer_cache_test.py: second identical guest question does not call Gemini; signed-in visitor always calls Gemini and never PUTs; refused (guarded) reply is not stored; cache endpoint down -> normal RAG answer.
features.notes: Lowest priority: drop it if the user only wants FAQ caching.
